handoff.purpose: Define lexing regex constants, property `embeds`, and helper functions for heading extraction, front matter stripping, slug generation, and anchor deduplication.

symbols.name: embeds
symbols.note: Returns tuple of DocLink objects whose embed attribute is True, filtered from self.links.

symbols.name: _ATX
symbols.note: Regex for ATX headings: 0-3 spaces, 1-6 '#' then whitespace or end, captures # count and optional title.

symbols.name: _ATX_CLOSE
symbols.note: Regex to strip trailing '#' from ATX heading title.

symbols.name: _SETEXT
symbols.note: Regex for setext headings: line of '=' or '-' with optional leading spaces.

symbols.name: _FENCE
symbols.note: Regex for fenced code blocks: 3+ backticks or tildes, optional info string.

symbols.name: _FRONT_MATTER
symbols.note: Regex for front matter delimiter: '---' or '+++'.

symbols.name: _NOT_SETEXT_TEXT
symbols.note: Regex for lines that cannot be setext heading text: list markers, blockquote, table separator, ATX start.

symbols.name: _INLINE_CODE
symbols.note: Regex for inline code spans: backtick-enclosed.

symbols.name: _INLINE_LINK
symbols.note: Regex for inline links excluding images, with optional title.

symbols.name: _REF_DEF
symbols.note: Regex for reference definition: [label]: <url> or url.

symbols.name: _AUTOLINK
symbols.note: Regex for autolinks: <scheme:...>.

symbols.name: _WIKILINK
symbols.note: Regex for Obsidian wikilinks, optional '!' for embed, captures '!' and link target.

symbols.name: _WIKI_DEFAULT_EXT
symbols.note: Default extension '.md' for wikilinks without explicit extension.

symbols.name: _SCHEME
symbols.note: Regex for URI scheme: alphabetic start, alphanumeric/plus/dot/hyphen.

symbols.name: _SLUG_STRIP
symbols.note: Regex to strip non-allowed characters for slug: anything not lowercase alphanumeric, space, underscore, hyphen.

symbols.name: _MD_LINK_TEXT
symbols.note: Regex to extract link text from markdown links for slug generation.

symbols.name: _MD_EMPHASIS
symbols.note: Regex to match emphasis markers: *, _, ~, `.

symbols.name: _strip_front_matter
symbols.note: Returns index of first content line after front matter; handles YAML/TOML delimiters.

symbols.name: slugify
symbols.note: Converts heading title to GitHub-style anchor slug, removing link markup and emphasis.

symbols.name: _headings
symbols.note: Returns list of (line_index, level, title) tuples for all headings, skipping fenced code blocks.

symbols.name: _dedup_anchors
symbols.note: Appends -1, -2, ... to duplicate slugs; first occurrence keeps original.

claims.text: CommonMark: 1-6 '#' at up to 3 columns of indent, then EITHER end-of-line OR whitespace. The whitespace requirement is load-bearing -- "#hashtag" and "#!/bin/sh" are NOT headings, and treating them as one fabricates structure.
claims.why: _ATX regex matches 0-3 spaces, then 1-6 '#', then requires optional whitespace or end-of-line via (?:[ \t]+(.*?))?[ \t]*$ which effectively ensures that if there is more text after the #, it must be preceded by whitespace. '#hashtag' has no space after '#', so _ATX would match '#', but then group(2) would be None, and the line would be considered a heading with empty title, which is a false positive. However, the regex does not enforce whitespace after the # if there is no trailing content; it would match a lone '#' line. The claim states that '#hashtag' is NOT a heading, but the regex would match it as a level-1 heading with title 'hashtag' because group(2) captures 'hashtag' after the space? Actually '#hashtag' has no space after '#', so _ATX.match('#hashtag') would match '#' as the hash group, but then (?:[ \t]+(.*?))? requires at least one whitespace before capturing the title; it would not match because there is no whitespace after '#'. So the match would be only the '#' and group(2) would be None, and the title would be empty. So the line '#hashtag' would be treated as an H1 with empty title, which is still wrong. The regex does not fully enforce the whitespace requirement; it only requires whitespace if there is a title. The comment says '#hashtag' is NOT a heading, but the regex would treat it as a heading (with empty title). Therefore the claim is broken in that the regex does not prevent false positives for lines like '#hashtag'.

claims.text: A closing sequence of '#'s is decoration, not part of the title.
claims.why: _ATX_CLOSE regex matches trailing spaces and hashes, and is used to strip them from the title in _headings.

claims.text: Without this, a table separator or a list item followed by a '---' rule becomes a fabricated H2.
claims.why: _NOT_SETEXT_TEXT regex matches lines starting with list markers, blockquote, table separator, or ATX start, preventing them from being considered setext heading text.

claims.text: The (?<!\!) guard keeps "![alt](img.png)" out: an image is an asset reference, not a document-to-document relation.
claims.why: _INLINE_LINK regex uses (?<!!) negative lookbehind, so '![alt](img.png)' does not match.

claims.text: Reference DEFINITION: "[label]: dest".  Definitions are counted as links of the document because that is what they are -- a declared destination.  Matching every reference USAGE back to its label is deliberately not attempted: it would double-count the same destination and buys no new edge.
claims.why: The comment describes intent about counting, but the actual counting logic is not in this chunk; only the regex is defined. The regex matches reference definitions, but whether they are counted as links is not visible.

claims.text: Bare autolink <https://...>; carried so external link COUNTS are honest.
claims.why: The regex is defined, but the counting logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: The inner text may not contain a bracket or a newline: ``[[a]`` and a ``[[`` left open at end of line are NOT links, and completing them for the author would invent an edge out of a typo. Nested brackets are excluded for the same reason -- there is no unambiguous reading of ``[[a[[b]]]]``, so there is no link in it.
claims.why: _WIKILINK regex matches '!?' then '[[', then captures [^\[\]\n]+, which excludes brackets and newlines, so nested brackets and open brackets at end of line are not matched.

claims.text: Default extension for a doc->doc wikilink: a vault is a folder of .md files, and ``[[Note]]`` means ``Note.md``. Tried ONLY when the literal name matches nothing, so ``![[diagram.png]]`` still means the png.
claims.why: The constant is defined, but the logic to apply default extension is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Index of the first content line, skipping YAML/TOML front matter.
claims.why: Function returns index after front matter; returns 0 if no front matter or unterminated.

claims.text: Unterminated front matter: treat the '---' as a thematic rule and parse the whole file, rather than swallowing the document silently.
claims.why: When front matter is not closed, function returns 0, so no lines are skipped.

claims.text: GitHub-style anchor slug for a heading (no de-duplication).
claims.why: Function produces slug similar to GitHub's anchor generation, without dedup.

claims.text: (line_index, level, title) for every heading, in document order. Fenced code is skipped: a '#' comment inside a ``` block is Python, not an H1, and indexing it would put shell/Python comments into the heading tree.
claims.why: Function iterates lines, tracks fence state, skips lines inside fences, and outputs headings in order.

claims.text: The heading is the PREVIOUS line; if it was already claimed by an ATX match this rule does not fire (ATX is checked first and would have consumed it).
claims.why: Code checks that previous line is not already in out (out[-1][0] != i-1) and ATX is checked before setext.

claims.text: GitHub's duplicate-anchor rule: first wins, later ones get -1, -2, ...
claims.why: Function is defined but its implementation is not fully visible (chunk ends after docstring).

observations.what: Property `embeds` returns a tuple of DocLink objects from self.links where embed is True. The type hint suggests DocLink is a namedtuple or similar.
_ATX regex matches lines like '#hashtag' as a heading with empty title, contrary to the comment that says it should not be a heading.
_headings function uses `i > start` to prevent setext heading detection on the first line after front matter; if a setext heading appears exactly at line `start`, it is missed.
_dedup_anchors function is defined but not used in this chunk; its behavior cannot be verified.
Fence closing condition uses `not fence_hit.group(2).strip()`, which may incorrectly close a fence if the info string contains only whitespace.
